With the November 3 midterm elections days away, the probe has intensified Trump's long-running feud with the Minnesota Democrat. Advertisement Somalia-born US congresswoman Ilhan Omar is a vocal critic of President Donald Trump, with repeated clashes over immigration, fraud allegations and his treatment of Somali Americans. (Images: AFP) By: India Today World Desk New Delhi , Oct 21, 2026 21:36 IST Last Updated Oct 21, 2026 21:36 IST Published by Anand Singh Oct 21, 2026 21:36 IST Written By Anand Singh Ilhan Omar, the Somalia-born US congresswoman who has been a frequent target of US President Donald Trump, is facing a federal citizenship probe that has taken a drastic turn. Investigators have reportedly obtained her DNA and seized her passport after searching her Washington home on October 12 . With the midterm elections on November 3 just less than two weeks away, Trump has said Omar could be deported or jailed. advertisement ❮ ❯ Read Full Story "I think she's a sick, a very dishonest person who hates our country," Trump said during an Oval Office event. Calling Omar "a disgrace to our country", he added that she "could also go to jail." The investigation is reportedly examining allegations about her age on immigration documents filed decades ago, but authorities have not publicly explained what the reported DNA evidence is meant to establish. The New York Post reported that investigators have obtained DNA evidence as part of an inquiry into allegations that Omar married her brother and committed immigration fraud . These allegations remain unproven. According to the newspaper, investigators are examining DNA evidence, government records and information from whistleblowers to determine whether Omar and members of her family committed immigration fraud. Fox News congressional correspondent Bill Melugin said on X that investigators had the DNA and passport as "evidence". He added that the passport issued through Omar's congressional office had not been retrieved and that authorities did not believe she had fled the country. In a video message shared after the raid, Omar appealed directly to supporters for continued financial help, thanking those who had already given money to her campaign, and urging others to contribute whatever they could. She described the coming period as "very expensive and challenging", framed the federal action as an attempt to intimidate her and other critics ahead of the midterms, and insisted she would not be silenced or deterred from campaigning. WHAT IS ILHAN OMAR'S CITIZENSHIP PROBE ABOUT? The investigation centres on allegations that Omar or her late father might have provided inaccurate information about her age on immigration documents decades ago. The question is whether any discrepancy could have affected her eligibility for US citizenship through her father. Born in Somalia, Omar arrived in the US as a child after spending time in a refugee camp in Kenya. She became a US citizen in 2000. Under US immigration law, certain children born outside the country can acquire citizenship through a parent who becomes a US citizen, subject to conditions including age, lawful permanent residency and custody. The allegations concerning Omar's immigration history have circulated for years. However, the existence of an investigation does not establish that she committed fraud or that her citizenship can be revoked. The government would need to establish a legal basis for any action against her citizenship, and such a move could be challenged in court. advertisement Omar has rejected the allegations and described the search as political intimidation. Her lawyers have also challenged the seizure of her belongings and demanded their return, arguing that there was no legitimate basis for the investigation, reported CBS News. Reports have said agents took her phone and other materials during the search. A separate report by Fox News said investigators had obtained DNA evidence, but it remains unclear from publicly available information how the sample was collected or what it is intended to establish. Claims that agents obtained it by "searching garbage bins" have been disputed by reports. The authorities have not publicly detailed the evidence or explained its relevance to the citizenship enquiry. Congressional Correspondent for Fox News, Bill Melugin, said US authorities aren't concerned that Ilhan Omar has fled the country. TRUMP'S LONG-RUNNING FEUD WITH OMAR Omar, the first Somali American elected to the US Congress, has been one of Trump's most persistent targets. The President has repeatedly attacked her in public, questioned her loyalty to the US, and made disparaging remarks about Somalia. He has also previously promoted unsubstantiated allegations about her personal life. advertisement Trump has now suggested that Omar could be deported, while also saying she could go to jail. On the other hand, former US president Barack Obama on October 18 publicly defended Omar, criticising the federal enquiry as an alarming use of government power against an elected official who has been outspoken in her opposition to Trump. Obama argued that pursuing a lawmaker over an unsubstantiated theory about her citizenship could set a troubling precedent for future administrations. The White House, however, has denied that the investigation is politically motivated. The administration has maintained that the Justice Department is focussed on enforcing the law and protecting public safety. Ilhan Omar has also drawn criticism in India for her positions on Kashmir, particularly her 2022 visit to Pakistan-occupied Kashmir, which New Delhi condemned as a violation of India's territorial integrity. She has also criticised India's handling of Jammu and Kashmir following the abrogation of Article 370 and raised allegations of discrimination against Muslims. She also introduced a resolution in the US Congress in June 2022 seeking to designate India a Country of Particular Concern over alleged religious freedom violations. advertisement WHY THE TIMING OF ILHAN OMAR'S CASE MATTERS The search of Omar's home took place a fortnight before the November midterm elections, in which she is seeking re-election in Minnesota. It must be noted that Trump's approval ratings have been at a record low due to the Iran war and inflation in the US. Following the raid, Omar's campaign issued urgent fundraising appeals urging supporters to contribute any sum they could manage — whether $5, $10 or $20, or whatever amount they felt able to give — calling the probe political intimidation. Critics quickly called the appeals "begging". The fundraising appeals, however, have drawn financial support from allies, but the specifics of how much money has been raised are not publicly known. Omar's public absence since the search has also fuelled speculation about her whereabouts. However, reports citing Fox News said members of her family had been seen at the Washington residence, while her husband had also been seen in public. Authorities, according to Fox News, were reportedly not concerned that she had left the country. advertisement With the midterms approaching, the probe against Omar and Trump's escalating threats have added to an already bitter political battle, with its legal and electoral consequences yet to unfold. - Ends (Written by Anand Singh) IN THIS STORY # United States of America # Donald Trump Advertisement Also Watch How is Lawrence Bishnoi able to operate from jail? Attending Kenya’s Mashujaa Day celebrations as President William Ruto’s guest of honour, Abiy emphasized the longstanding partnership between the two countries, highlighting cooperation in electricity, telecommunications, trade and regional connectivity. Yet beyond the diplomatic celebrations, the visit coincided with growing tensions involving Somalia, whose internal political crisis has begun complicating its relations with both Ethiopia and Kenya. Although Abiy’s visit was officially centered on Kenya’s Mashujaa Day celebrations and bilateral cooperation, it unfolded against a backdrop of growing regional tensions involving Somalia. The visit did not publicly establish a common Ethiopian and Kenyan position on the Somali crisis, but it brought renewed attention to the strategic importance of their partnership as both countries navigate increasingly complicated relations with Mogadishu. The significance of Ethiopia’s relationship with Kenya extends beyond bilateral cooperation. Both countries have invested considerable military and diplomatic resources in Somalia’s stabilization, particularly in efforts to contain Al Shabaab and prevent insecurity from spreading across their borders. However, Somalia’s confrontation between its federal government and regional political actors is creating disagreements over the responsibilities of neighbouring countries. For Ethiopia, the challenge is to maintain its commitment to Somalia’s security without becoming involved in political disputes that could undermine its wider regional interests. The immediate source of tension lies in Somalia’s South West State, where the removal of former regional president Abdiaziz Hassan Mohamed Laftagareen in March 2026 failed to produce a lasting political settlement. Instead, confrontations between his supporters and forces aligned with the federal government have continued, exposing deeper disagreements over regional autonomy and the distribution of political authority. By October 19, forces loyal to Laftagareen reportedly controlled five towns in the Bay region, including Buurhakaba, Qansaxdheere and Dinsoor, complicating Mogadishu’s efforts to consolidate authority. The conflict is particularly consequential because the South West State includes territories where Ethiopian forces have maintained a security presence for years. According to Somali Guardian reporting published on October 19 , Somali federal authorities requested Ethiopian military assistance against forces aligned with Laftagareen, but Ethiopian commanders declined to participate in what they considered an internal political confrontation. Although the reported exchange has not been independently confirmed, it illustrates a fundamental question concerning foreign military involvement in Somalia: whether security assistance intended to confront common threats should extend to supporting the federal government in disputes over domestic political authority. For Ethiopia, the issue has acquired additional importance following the transition from the African Union Transition Mission in Somalia, ATMIS, to the African Union Support and Stabilization Mission in Somalia, AUSSOM, which commenced on January 1, 2025. Under United Nations Security Council Resolution 2767 , the successor mission was authorized to support Somali forces against Al Shabaab, protect civilians and facilitate the gradual transfer of security responsibilities to Somali institutions. Its mandate also encompasses security support for political processes, but does not provide unrestricted authority to determine the outcome of internal political disputes. The transition brought renewed attention to the distinction between Ethiopian troops operating under African Union arrangements and those deployed through separate bilateral security understandings. This distinction matters because forces assigned to AUSSOM operate within a defined multinational framework, while deployments outside that structure depend on separate arrangements with Somalia. In its December 2025 communiqué , the African Union Peace and Security Council explicitly acknowledged Ethiopia and Uganda for deploying additional troops under bilateral arrangements. Their presence cannot therefore be understood solely through AUSSOM’s command structure. Ethiopia’s longstanding involvement in Somalia has primarily been driven by the need to prevent Al Shabaab from developing secure operating areas near Ethiopian territory. The group’s ability to exploit instability and threaten communities across borders makes developments in Somalia directly relevant to Ethiopia’s national security. Ethiopian military operations and participation in successive African Union missions have consequently contributed to a broader effort to contain threats before they reach Ethiopian territory. The South West State remains especially important because the Bay and Bakool regions form part of the wider security environment connected to Ethiopia’s eastern frontier. Participation in Somalia’s internal political confrontations, however, would expose Ethiopia to different risks. Military intervention could associate Ethiopian forces with one Somali political faction, weaken relationships with local communities and transform a defined security commitment into an extended responsibility for political outcomes. Even a successful intervention would not necessarily resolve disagreements concerning federal authority and regional political representation. Somalia’s domestic disputes require political settlements that military involvement by neighbouring countries cannot independently deliver. This position should not be confused with opposition to Somalia’s federal government. Addis Ababa and Mogadishu continue to maintain diplomatic relations and share an interest in preventing renewed militant expansion. Somali President Hassan Sheikh Mohamud’s September 29 visit to Addis Ababa , during which he discussed bilateral relations and regional security with Abiy Ahmed, demonstrated the continued importance of diplomatic engagement despite existing disagreements. Those disagreements nevertheless have a deeper history. The January 2024 memorandum of understanding between Ethiopia and Somaliland, which addressed potential Ethiopian maritime access, produced a significant confrontation with Mogadishu over sovereignty and territorial integrity. Somalia regarded the arrangement as an infringement on its sovereignty, while Ethiopia viewed access to the sea as an important strategic and economic objective. The dispute contributed to Somalia’s closer security engagement with Egypt, which already maintained long winded Nile disagreements with Ethiopia. The December 2024 Ankara Declaration , facilitated by Türkiye, helped restore diplomatic engagement by reaffirming mutual respect for sovereignty and acknowledging the possibility of mutually beneficial maritime arrangements under Somalia’s sovereign authority. Nevertheless, restoring diplomatic communication did not eliminate competing regional security calculations. Egypt’s expanding security engagement with Somalia and its prospective contribution to AUSSOM have introduced further sensitivity into discussions about troop deployments. The African Union’s June 2025 negotiations with troop-contributing countries included Ethiopia and Egypt, demonstrating that both countries were considered within the mission’s institutional arrangements. In December 2025, the African Union also acknowledged Egypt’s preparations for deployment while emphasizing the need to prevent security gaps during the transition. Political endorsement, negotiated contributions and actual troop deployments, however, remain distinct stages. For Ethiopia, any substantial expansion of Egyptian forces near areas where Ethiopian troops operate would raise operational questions, particularly given the unresolved Nile dispute. Careful coordination would be essential to prevent competing strategic interests from complicating counterterrorism operations. Kenya faces a related challenge arising from Somalia’s domestic political confrontation. Laftagareen’s presence in Kenya following his removal has generated criticism from Somali officials. On October 19, Somalia’s parliamentary speaker, Abdikadir Mohamed Nur Jama, reportedly accused individuals residing in Kenya of involvement in activities connected to the conflict and questioned the alleged protection they received. The reporting did not establish evidence supporting those allegations, and Kenyan authorities had not publicly responded at the time. Hosting Somali political figures does not independently demonstrate Kenyan government support for their military activities. Nairobi must balance its diplomatic responsibilities and continued cooperation with Mogadishu against its own legal and national security considerations. The consequences of Somali instability for Kenya are also economic. The Lamu Port South Sudan Ethiopia Transport corridor, LAPSSET, represents an important regional infrastructure initiative intended to expand commercial connectivity and diversify access to maritime trade. Its security is connected to conditions in northern and coastal Kenya, where Al Shabaab has demonstrated the ability to threaten personnel and transport infrastructure. On September 19, 2026, suspected militants attacked Kenyan military personnel patrolling part of the corridor in Garissa. No casualties were reported, but the incident illustrated the security demands associated with protecting strategic infrastructure. Although these attacks cannot be directly attributed to the South West State’s political crisis, prolonged instability in Somalia could place additional pressure on counterterrorism operations and create opportunities for militant expansion. For Kenya, preserving security cooperation with Somalia therefore carries implications for domestic security, investment and regional transport connectivity. Ethiopia shares an interest in protecting these connections, which could strengthen economic integration and provide additional commercial routes. Against this background, the partnership between Addis Ababa and Nairobi offers continuity. Cooperation in electricity transmission, telecommunications and transport has created practical interests that extend beyond individual political disagreements. During his October 20 visit , Abiy emphasized Ethiopia’s electricity exports to Kenya, Safaricom’s presence in Ethiopia and growing commercial connections. Their importance becomes greater as Ethiopia confronts renewed tensions with Eritrea, instability in northern Ethiopia and unresolved strategic disagreements with Egypt. The October 2026 escalation in Tigray and tensions with Eritrea demonstrate the competing pressures confronting Addis Ababa. Strong relations with Kenya provide an additional channel for diplomatic consultation without requiring both governments to adopt identical policies toward Somalia. The coming months will test whether the three countries can prevent Somalia’s internal confrontation from developing into a wider regional dispute. Particular attention should be given to the security situation around Baidoa, changes to Ethiopian and Egyptian troop arrangements, and Somalia’s political preparations ahead of the presidential election announced for May 15, 2027 . Diplomatic engagement through Kenya, IGAD or other regional mechanisms could become increasingly relevant if political divisions deepen. Whether mediation initiatives emerge, however, will depend on the willingness of the parties to pursue negotiation. Abiy’s Kenya visit ultimately illustrates the continuing value of dependable regional partnerships during a period of uncertainty. Ethiopia’s national interests require a stable Somalia, effective cooperation against Al Shabaab and security arrangements that do not unnecessarily entangle Ethiopian forces in domestic political rivalries. Its relationship with Kenya offers opportunities to advance those objectives while protecting economic integration and regional connectivity. The challenge for Addis Ababa is to preserve this partnership alongside constructive engagement with Mogadishu, ensuring that Somalia’s political disagreements do not become another source of confrontation across the Horn of Africa. A comparison of the IGAD facilitated process that produced the 1988 agreement with the Turkish brokered Ankara Declaration of December 2024 reveals both the continuity of Ethiopia’s core security interests and the shifting diplomatic environment in which those interests are pursued. The confrontation that shaped the 1980s negotiations originated in the aftermath of the 1977–78 Ogaden War. Somalia continued to assert territorial claims over the Ogaden region of Ethiopia. Mutual destabilization compounded by internal pressures on both regimes produced a protracted period of tension short of renewed full scale interstate war. At the inaugural IGAD summit in Djibouti in January 1986 Ethiopian leader Mengistu Haile Mariam and Somali President Siad Barre established a joint ad hoc ministerial committee to examine the sources of bilateral discord. Although the committee was formally joint Ethiopia’s representatives led at key sessions by Foreign Minister Lt-Col. Goshu Wolde consistently prioritized recognition of existing international boundaries and the cessation of support for anti Ethiopian groups. This agenda setting approach shaped the substance of the talks. Somalia preferred to sequence confidence building measures troop disengagement restoration of diplomatic relations and prisoner exchanges before addressing the boundary question. Three principal ministerial sessions took place in May 1986 August 1986 and April 1987. Progress remained limited because of these differing priorities. A further meeting between the two heads of state on the margins of the March 1988 IGAD summit in Djibouti provided the decisive political impetus. The resulting agreement formalized after talks in Mogadishu on 3 and 4 April 1988 restored diplomatic relations provided for the withdrawal of security forces from the border ended hostile propaganda terminated mutual support for insurgent groups and arranged the exchange of prisoners of war. Both sides agreed to discuss the boundary question at a later date. In practice the accord ended active Somali claims on the Ogaden and secured Ethiopia’s south eastern frontier freeing Ethiopian resources for pressing internal challenges. The 1988 agreement demonstrated that a regional structure could deliver tangible results when the parties shared a pragmatic interest in stabilizing a disputed border and when one party Ethiopia articulated its security requirements with clarity and consistency. No open interstate war between Ethiopia and Somalia occurred after 1988. Somalia’s subsequent state collapse created a different environment. Under Prime Minister Meles Zenawi Ethiopia engaged constructively in efforts to rebuild Somali institutions helping to shape the transitional federal structure that emerged in the absence of a functioning central authority. This engagement responded first to immediate security concerns arising from the political space along Ethiopia’s border. At the same time it reinforced Ethiopia’s standing as a constructive regional actor. When the Islamic Courts Union consolidated control over much of southern Somalia in 2006 and posed a direct security challenge Ethiopia intervened in support of the Transitional Federal Government. Limited deployments earlier that year preceded full scale action in December 2006. That intervention reflected continuity rather than rupture Ethiopia acted to prevent hostile forces from establishing themselves in adjacent ungoverned space. Serious bilateral tension re emerged only in 2024 following the January memorandum of understanding between Ethiopia and Somaliland concerning commercial and naval access to the sea. Somalia denounced the arrangement as a violation of its territorial integrity, recalled its ambassador and explicitly rejected African Union mediation efforts conditioning any engagement on Ethiopia’s retraction of the memorandum. This stance effectively limited the immediate scope for regional bodies including IGAD to facilitate dialogue on a dispute touching core sovereignty claims. The political climate had become more transactional with parties weighing concrete exchanges of interests rather than operating within the denser shared outlooks of earlier periods. The Ankara Declaration of 11–12 December 2024 facilitated by Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, produced a de escalation. The leaders reaffirmed respect for each other’s sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity. They acknowledged the potential benefits of Ethiopia’s assured access to and from the sea while affirming that any commercial arrangements would operate under the sovereign authority of the Federal Republic of Somalia. Technical negotiations were scheduled to begin no later than the end of February 2025 and to conclude within four months with Turkish facilitation available as needed. IGAD welcomed the declaration as a constructive step toward regional stability that external facilitation can complement rather than displace regional mechanisms when circumstances require additional diplomatic weight. In the mid 1980s member state cohesion a bipolar international context that channeled regional diplomacy and a shared interest in border stability enabled IGAD to serve as an effective vehicle. Ethiopia acting within that institutional framework advanced outcomes consistent with its security requirements. Three decades later protracted state fragility in Somalia internal challenges across several Horn countries and the proliferation of external actors with diverse interests altered the diplomacy. Regional organizations continue to perform important roles however on certain sovereignty laden disputes their immediate leverage may be constrained. Ethiopia’s posture has remained consistent across these decades safeguarding the south eastern frontier preventing the establishment of hostile actors in adjacent ungoverned spaces and securing reliable access to the sea. The instruments joint committees under a regional umbrella support for transitional governance calibrated military engagement when necessary and pragmatic external facilitation have adapted to changing conditions. In 2024 Turkish mediation filled a temporary institutional vacuum created by the particular constraints facing regional mechanisms on this sovereignty sensitive question. The 1988 accord and the 2024 Ankara Declaration both illustrate that durable progress depends less on the formal identity of the mediator than on the alignment of core interests and the availability of credible channels for dialogue. Convened in late 1996 under IGAD’s newly established conflict-resolution mandate, the talks culminated on 3 January 1997 in the creation of a 41-member National Salvation Council, with representation allocated to the four major clan families and smaller communities. Although Sodere did not produce a lasting government, it established a broad-based framework for political representation that subsequent reconciliation efforts would revisit The collapse of the Somali state in January 1991 left political authority dispersed among armed factions, while successive international efforts failed to establish a national government capable of consolidating control. The Addis Ababa Agreement of 1993 brought leading factions into a common framework, but agreement on paper did not resolve the struggle for power in Mogadishu; by the time the last United Nations troops withdrew in March 1995, the underlying competition remained intact. Rivalry between Ali Mahdi Mohamed and the Aideed camp, which passed to Hussein Aideed following General Mohamed Farah Aideed’s death in August 1996, continued to obstruct the emergence of a national political authority. The consequences extended beyond the capital. In the border region of Gedo, Al-Itihaad al-Islamiya (AIAI) established a presence centered on Luuq, roughly ninety kilometers from Ethiopia, which Addis Ababa regarded as a base for a movement responsible for attacks inside Ethiopia and linked to other armed groups opposed to its government. Somalia’s fragmentation thus presented Ethiopia with a problem that international mediation alone had not resolved, the absence of a functioning state was not merely prolonging conflict within Somalia but also leaving neighboring territory exposed to armed networks that could operate across the border. This gave Ethiopia a direct security interest in the restoration of Somali political authority. The expansion of regional institutions in 1996 provided an important foundation for a more coordinated response to Somalia’s political fragmentation, creating a framework through which Ethiopia could address its security concerns while contributing to a regional effort to restore Somali political dialogue. Founded in 1986 as the Intergovernmental Authority on Drought and Development, with a mandate centred on drought and desertification, the organization was reconstituted as the Intergovernmental Authority on Development (IGAD) following the amendment of its founding instrument in Nairobi on 21 March 1996 and its relaunch at the Djibouti summit of 25–26 November. The revised charter incorporated the prevention, management and resolution of inter-state and intra-state conflicts through dialogue, placing peace and security alongside food security and economic cooperation among the organization’s priorities. This change reflected a broader recognition that the conflicts confronting the Horn of Africa required regional mechanisms capable of addressing their political and security dimensions. For Ethiopia, whose border security was directly affected by the absence of effective authority in Somalia, IGAD’s expanded mandate offered a legitimate avenue for supporting reconciliation through regional diplomacy. The framework connected Ethiopia’s immediate security concerns with the wider regional interest in reducing conflict and restoring political order in Somalia, giving its diplomatic engagement an institutional foundation and a shared regional purpose. Although divisions among IGAD members, including the severance of relations with Sudan by Ethiopia, Eritrea and Uganda during the preceding year, complicated regional cooperation, the organization’s expanded mandate established an important basis for renewed engagement. OAU strengthened this framework in July 1996, when its Yaoundé resolution recognized Meles Zenawi, then outgoing OAU chairman, as holding a special mandate to facilitate peace in Somalia and supported efforts by IGAD member states to reactivate their initiatives. This endorsement connected the emerging regional effort to the OAU’s broader diplomatic role and reinforced the legitimacy of renewed attempts to bring Somali factions into negotiations. Ethiopia subsequently informed the United Nations Security Council that it had convened the Sodere conference in November 1996 in accordance with an IGAD mandate. Operating within this reinforced regional framework, Ethiopian conduct in the second half of 1996 ran along two tracks that differed in instrument yet converged through local partnerships. On the military track, Ethiopia acted against Al-Itihaad al-Islamiya (AIAI), an Islamist group that had established a presence in the Gedo region centered on Luuq, roughly ninety kilometres from the Ethiopian border. Addis Ababa regarded AIAI as a direct security threat, holding it responsible for attacks inside Ethiopia and linking it to other armed networks opposed to the Ethiopian government. Ethiopian forces therefore crossed into Gedo on 9 August 1996 to attack AIAI bases, and fighting continued through December. The fourth major assault on the group, launched on 11 June 1997, captured Luuq and Buulo Haawo and deprived AIAI of its last major bases in the region. This military campaign ran in parallel with a political initiative that sought to harness Somali opposition to AIAI and embed Ethiopia’s border-security objectives within a broader reconciliation process. On the political track, Ethiopia convened Somali leaders at the Sodere resort for roughly six weeks of talks, which ended on 3 January 1997 with a declaration signed by 27 leaders representing 26 factions. The declaration created a National Salvation Council of 41 members and a National Executive Committee of 11 members led by five co-chairmen, with authority to speak for the Council and to prepare a Transitional Central Authority or Provisional Central Government, and it committed the signatories to a National Reconciliation Conference at Bossaso. The Somali National Front, a competitor of AIAI for control of Gedo, was among the signatories. That overlap offered Somali opponents of AIAI an institutional route to national standing and tied a border security objective to a political process that Somali actors could own. The composition of the Council contains the process’s most durable contribution. Nine seats went to each of the four major clan families, Darod, Hawiye, Rahanweyn and Dir, and five to smaller groups, a distribution that totals 41 and approximates the half-share later formalized for minorities under the 4.5 formula. For the first time the Darod accepted parity among the main clan families. That principle of clan-family parity, first given institutional expression at Sodere, was subsequently formalized at the Arta conference in 2000 and then applied at scale by the Mbagathi process, which in 2004 allocated 61 seats to each of the four major families and 31 to the minority bloc within a 275-member Transitional Federal Parliament. By converting a contest over who speaks for Somalia into a bounded negotiation over who sits within each family’s allotment, parity supplied the mechanism through which Sodere moved Somali politics from open military competition toward transitional institutions. Sodere’s significance extended beyond the representational framework it helped establish to the regional diplomacy through which that framework was pursued. Ethiopia’s subsequent involvement in Somali reconciliation formed part of a recurring pattern that included hosting the 1993 Addis Ababa conference, convening Sodere in 1996 and 1997, participating in the IGAD-mediated Mbagathi talks that produced the Transitional Federal Charter in 2004, and contributing troops to the African Union missions in Somalia, AMISOM and ATMIS, and now AUSSOM. The Mbagathi record offers particularly clear evidence that Somali actors themselves regarded Ethiopia’s participation as consequential. In February 2004, six faction leaders of the Somali Restoration and Reconstruction Council announced that they would stay out of the final phase of the talks while Ethiopia was absent from the table. Hussein Aideed, who had succeeded his father General Mohamed Farah Aideed in 1996 and had remained outside the Sodere process the following year, now argued that a regional peace process required consensus among neighbouring states as well as among Somalis. His position marked a shift from contesting Ethiopia’s involvement in 1997 to treating the participation of neighboring states as a condition of a credible settlement, illustrating how the regional approach embodied at Sodere became an established feature of subsequent Somali peace negotiations. This historical experience has direct relevance as Somalia confronts a demanding security transition, with Al-Shabaab continuing to threaten state consolidation, domestic political negotiations remaining unsettled after the inconclusive May 2026 talks, and AUSSOM’s operational future facing growing financial uncertainty following Washington’s announced intention to end its support for UN logistics and operations from 2027. Ethiopia’s renewed commitment to AUSSOM, reaffirmed at the August 2026 troop-contributing countries summit, provides an important basis for strengthening this regional security relationship. Somalia’s current security transition increases the strategic importance of sustained coordination with Ethiopia. Al-Shabaab retains a presence in areas of Gedo and Bakool near the Ethiopian frontier, while Washington’s decision to end funding for UN logistical support to AUSSOM after December 2026 adds pressure to the mission’s operational continuity. These developments connect Somalia’s internal security challenges directly to the management of its western border, where gaps in territorial control can enable armed groups to move, reorganize and exploit weaknesses in coordination between security forces. Ethiopia’s direct exposure to these threats, its existing security involvement in Somalia and its capacity to operate along the shared frontier make bilateral cooperation consequential to how these risks are managed. For Mogadishu, the practical priority is to establish predictable arrangements with Addis Ababa for intelligence exchange, border threat assessment, troop coordination and consultation over operations affecting Somali territory. These mechanisms would help align Ethiopian security activities with federal priorities, improve continuity between bilateral cooperation and AUSSOM, and give Somali authorities greater influence over the regional response to threats within their jurisdiction. As Somalia assumes greater responsibility for its own security amid uncertainty over international support, the quality of its coordination with Ethiopia will directly affect its capacity to manage cross-border threats and sustain security across its western regions. football.content: الهلال السوداني يدعم صفوفه بصفقة متميزة في ختام الميركاتو الهلال السوداني يدعم صفوفه بصفقة متميزة في ختام الميركاتو مباريات اليوم لاعبو فريق الهلال السوداني (Facebook/Alhilalsc.official) 20 أكتوبر 2026 الهلال السوداني يدعم صفوفه بصفقة متميزة في ختام الميركاتو الهلال السوداني دوري أبطال أفريقيا كرة قدم حافظ محمد أحمد الخرطوم winwin أعلن نادي الهلال السوداني، اليوم الثلاثاء 20 أكتوبر/ تشرين الأول، تعاقده مع المهاجم الموريتاني أحمد أحمد قادما من نادي نواذيبو، بعقد يمتد لخمسة أعوام، في ختام صفقات النادي خلال الميركاتو الصيفي. ويأتي انضمام مهاجم "المرابطون" ليعزز الخط الهجومي للفريق إلى جانب مواطنه أحمد سالم مبارك، وذلك استجابة للمناشدات الجماهيرية المستمرة، التي طالبت بتدعيم هذا المركز. زينباور يتنفس الصعداء بعد تلبية مطالبه وتكون إدارة "الموج الأزرق" برئاسة هشام السوباط مطالب مدرب الفريق، قد لبّت طلبات المدرب جوزيف زينباور، في ظل تراجع مستوى قائد الفريق محمد عبد الرحمن وزميله صنداي أودتونجي. وتجدر الإشارة إلى أن المدرب الذي يبلغ من 56 عاما، قد ألمح إلى عدم قناعته بمستوى اللاعب الليبيري إيمانويل فلومو، من خلال تحويله إلى صفوف الفريق الرديف. أحمد أحمد يدعم صفوف الهلال سيستهل المهاجم الموريتاني الذي يبلغ من العمر 23 عاما مسيرته مع "النادي الأزرق"، عقب مباراة الإياب ضد سيداما بونا الإثيوبي في الدور التمهيدي الثاني لبطولة دوري أبطال أفريقيا . اقرأ أيضًا الهلال السوداني يصنع الحدث و"غربال" على موعد مع المجد حرب تصريحات.. الهلال السوداني يرد على رئيس اتحاد الكرة! وسينضم اللاعب إلى تشكيلة الفريق في الدوري الرواندي، بانتظار تأهيله للعب في دور المجموعات حال التأهل، حيث سينافس زميليه عبد الرحمن وصنداي أودتونجي على مركزه. ويستعد الهلال أحد عمالقة الدوري السوداني ، لمواجهة الإياب أمام سيداما بونا الإثيوبي، المقررة يوم الأحد 25 أكتوبر/ تشرين الأول على ملعب "أماهورو" في العاصمة كيغالي؛ علما أن الفريق قطع شوطا كبيرا نحو التأهل بعد فوزه ذهابا بهدفين من دون رد. أخبار ذات صلة الهلال السوداني حرب تصريحات.. الهلال السوداني يرد على رئيس اتحاد الكرة! السوداني لكرة القدم، خلال مؤتمره الصحفي الأخير، ردود فعل غاضبة بعد أن حمّل نادي الهلال السوداني مسؤولية خسارة المنتخب الوطني أمام نظيره الموزمبيقي في تصفيات كأس أمم أفريقيا . واستنكرت إدارة الفريق الأزرق تبرير رئيس الاتحاد، الذي أرجع الهزيمة إلى تأخر انضمام لاعبي الفريق إلى معسكر "صقور الجديان"، نتيجة ارتباطهم بمباراة ودية أمام أهلي طرابلس الليبي، مما أربك ترتيبات سفرهم. إدارة الهلال السوداني تستنكر تصريحات سر الختم من جانبه، وصف رامي كمال، عضو مجلس إدارة الهلال السوداني تصريحات رئيس الاتحاد بأنها "جانبت الصواب" وتعد محاولة للهروب من المسؤولية، وشدد كمال على رفض النادي إقحامه في نتائج المنتخب، مؤكدًا أنّ الهلال ظل داعمًا للاتحاد السوداني انطلاقًا من مسؤوليته الوطنية وحرصه على مصلحة الكرة السودانية. كما دعا كمال إلى ضرورة تقييم نتائج المنتخب بناءً على أسس فنية وإدارية موضوعية، بعيدًا عن تحميل الأطراف الأخرى المسؤولية، أو إطلاق تصريحات قد تضر باستقرار المنظومة الكروية في البلاد. اقرأ أيضًا الهلال السوداني يصنع الحدث و"غربال" على موعد مع المجد اتحاد الكرة يحسم مستقبل مدرب منتخب السودان كواسي أبياه وأكد إداري الهلال السوداني إدراك الجميع للظروف الاستثنائية التي تعمل في ظلها منظومة كرة القدم السودانية، مشيرًا إلى أن ناديه جزء أصيل من هذه المنظومة، وأن مجلس إدارته يعمل بجد مع شركائه، وفي مقدمتهم الاتحاد السوداني لكرة القدم وبقية الأندية، لتجاوز التحديات الراهنة وضمان استمرارية النشاط الرياضي وتطويره. كما شدد على أنّ المرحلة الحالية تتطلب من جميع الأطراف التحلي بروح المسؤولية المشتركة، وتعزيز الحوار والتنسيق، والمشاركة الفاعلة في اتخاذ القرارات الاستراتيجية التي تخدم الكرة السودانية وتدفع بمسيرتها نحو الاستقرار، بدلًا من تبادل الاتهامات عبر وسائل الإعلام. واختتم بالتأكيد على أنّ رفضهم لتصريح رئيس الاتحاد لا يعني إنكار الجهود الإيجابية التي يبذلها الدكتور معتصم جعفر وأعضاء مجلس إدارته في دعم الأندية المشاركة في البطولات الأفريقية باسم السودان، مؤكدًا على أنّ اختلاف الرأي لا يلغي أهمية العمل المشترك لمصلحة الكرة السودانية، كما عبّر كمال عن ثقته بقدرة منتخب السودان على تجاوز كبوة مباراة موزمبيق، وتحقيق نتائج إيجابية في الاستحقاقات القادمة تضمن تأهله إلى football.summary: اقترب فريق الهلال السوداني وفريق السويحلي الليبي من التأهل إلى دور المجموعات في دوري أبطال أفريقيا بعد أدائهما القوي في التصفيات. حيث حقق الهلال السوداني فوزاً مهماً على منافسه في مباراة الذهاب، مما يعزز فرصه في التأهل. من جهة أخرى، قدم السويحلي الليبي عرضاً مميزاً في مباراته، مما يضعه في موقف جيد للتقدم في البطولة. يتطلع كلا الفريقين إلى تحقيق نتائج إيجابية في مباريات الإياب لضمان مكانهما في دور المجموعات، حيث تعتبر هذه المرحلة من البطولة ذات أهمية كبيرة للأندية الأفريقية.

football.content: نتائج ذهاب دور الـ32 من دوري أبطال أفريقيا | يلاكورة المباريات أخبار دوريات وبطولات مالتيميديا كلام فى الكورة TV 2026 جميع الحقوق محفوظة لدى السويحلي يسقط الترجي وتعادل صنداونز.. نتائج ذهاب دور الـ32 من دوري أبطال أفريقيا مباراة السويحلي مع الترجي كتب: مصطفى جمال الأحد 18 أكتوبر 2026 11:03 م 0 أقيمت اليوم الأحد عدة مواجهات مثيرة، في ذهاب دور الـ32 من بطولة دوري أبطال أفريقيا، جاء على رأسها انتصار السويحلي الليبي على حساب الترجي الرياضي التونسي، وتعادل ماميلودي صنداونز الجنوب إفريقي مع ويلييت الأنجولي. وتفوق السويحلي الليبي على ملعبه بهدف دون رد، على حساب الترجي التونسي، ليشعل المنافسة بين الفريقين على بطاقة الصعود لمرحلة المجموعات، قبل لقاء الإياب في تونس. وخرج ماميلودي صنداونز الجنوب إفريقي بتعادل سلبي أمام ويلييت الأنجولي، ليحافظ على نظافة شباكه خارج ملعبه، بينما انتصر الهلال السوداني على حساب سيداما بونا الإثيوبي بهدفين دون رد، ليضع قدمًا في مرحلة المجموعات. إعلان وفرط المغرب الفاسي في تقدمه أمام أسيك ميموزا الإيفواري، لينتهي اللقاء الذي أقيم في المغرب بالتعادل بنتيجة 1-1، بينما سقط مولودية الجزائر في فخ الهزيمة خارج ملعبه على يد إينوجو رينجرز، بهدفين دون رد. وخسر فريق بترو أتلتيكو الأنجولي بشكل مفاجئ خارج ملعبه، بثنائية نظيفة على يد سكوتلاند الزيمبابوي، وتغلب حوريا كوناكري الغيني على المريخ السوداني بهدف دون رد. وخطف فريق كولومب الكاميروني فوزًا ثمينًا خارج أرضه على ملعب تونجيث السنغالي، بثنائية نظيفة، ليقترب أكثر من الصعود للمرحلة المقبلة وهي دور المجموعات من دوري أبطال أفريقيا. دوري أبطال أفريقيا الترجي صنداونز السويحلي بترو أتلتيكو الهلال السوداني مولودية الجزائر المريخ السوداني المغرب الفاسي 0 نجم صنداونز: نستطيع التتويج مجددا بدوري الأبطال.. اللعب أمام جماهيرنا مختلف جولة الحسم.. مواعيد مباريات إياب الدور التمهيدي الثاني لدوري أبطال أفريقيا التعليقات دوري أبطال أفريقيا الأخبار ترتيب الفرق نتائج المباريات مالتيميديا شاهد كل المباريات
